subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Is source-level plausibility enough to change the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy now, or should OpenClaw require live or deterministic proof of a healthy-run false abort first?
rationale: The source path exists, but current tests intentionally rely on processing/no-activeWorkKind stale recovery and the reporter labels the healthy-run abort mechanism as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open for a controlled gateway log, harness repro, or Crabbox/live run showing state=processing, classification=stale_session_state, and abort_embedded_run on healthy work before changing policy.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow state-aware classifier change and require tests that preserve genuinely stale processing recovery while avoiding healthy-run aborts.

options.title: Fold into recovery redesign
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader stuck-session recovery ladder and event-loop liveness work instead of changing this classifier edge alone.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for a controlled gateway log, harness repro, or Crabbox/live run showing state=processing, classification=stale_session_state, and abort_embedded_run on healthy work before changing policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownerless-lane recovery work makes obviyus the best available routing candidate for the recovery-policy decision.
